rows.name: Agent activity diagram
rows.purpose: Aims to give developers one overview of where work happens: which agent works on which specification, on which branch, folder and machine.
rows.description: An agent activity diagram gives developers one picture of where what work is happening: which agents work on which specification of which project, on which branch and in which folder, and on what system. It has five element types: projects in the middle, then their specifications with their tasks listed by status, the agents working on them, the locations they work in (a branch and a folder, with the pull requests opened from it), and the environments those locations run on, such as a local machine, a cloud environment, a container or WSL. Four relations connect them, and nothing else: a project to its specifications, a specification to its agents, an agent to its locations and a location to its environment. Agents keep it current by editing one plain YAML file, `.aad`, as they work; a person reads it as a picture, locks what they place, folds away groups they do not need and shows or hides archived specifications. That view is kept in the same file, and agents leave it alone. An open diagram follows the file as agents change it.
rows.whySpecialized: Work spread over agents, branches, worktrees and machines is invisible in any one of them; a dedicated diagram that agents keep current, with fixed rules for what connects to what, makes it one picture.
rows.theory: A notation defined by the user of this repository, so ADP owns the schema and the `etalii/` origin rather than a standards body's

rows.name: Agent Behavior Modelling

rows.description: Agent Behavior Modelling uses Behavior Tree modelling to facilitate the creation of agent behavior descriptions. In stark contrast with text-only behavior modelling, diagram based Agent Behavior Modelling facilitates consistent definition and refinement of agent behavior.
rows.whySpecialized: Prose instructions hide their control flow; a behavior tree makes order, alternatives, loops and approval gates visible and checkable, while the Markdown file the agent reads stays plain text.
rows.theory: Behavior trees from game development and robotics, tuned to agent engineering; ADP owns the schema and the etalii/ origin

rows.name: Knowledge designer
rows.purpose: Model knowledge as linked tables of typed properties in local YAML, XML or JSON files, with views that sort, filter and group them.
rows.description: A designer that stores row and column based information in YAML, XML or JSON files. Inspired by Notion's database and other similar solutions, it brings the knowledge engineering capability to local systems. Its goal is to assist users with the modelling of knowledge, both for personal use and to facilitate human-tailored LLM knowledge engineering. Properties can quickly be generated and changed: text, numbers, dates and times, times, selections, multiple selections and more. Several such database files can be linked together by defining properties as (multi) directional relations. Each file also contains views, in which property visibility, sorting, filtering and row grouping (by parent, by a select property and so on) can be applied.
rows.whySpecialized: It brings the knowledge engineering of Notion's databases to local files: properties are quickly generated and changed, files are linked through (multi) directional relations, and views keep visibility, sorting, filtering and grouping beside the data, for personal use and for human-tailored LLM knowledge engineering.
rows.theory: After Notion's databases (typed properties, table views, relations) and similar solutions; ADP owns the schema and the etalii/ origin. Defined in etalii.adp as an FBL binding per format plus a DESL specification, so every host builds the same designer

rows.name: Sankey diagram

rows.description: Sankey diagram (nodes in columns joined by flows whose thickness follows their value, drawn as smooth translucent bands in the income-statement style of annual reports; domain agnostic, with a twelve-word colour palette or custom hex per node and flow, a thickness scale, values stepped in place, and nodes dragged within their column while the others make room; `.skv` — Sankey Diagram Visualization, ADP's own YAML schema, registered by an `.adp` file); `sankey`
rows.whySpecialized: A Sankey diagram's meaning is in its proportions: flow thickness must follow value, columns must balance and bands must curve cleanly between stacked bars, which a generic canvas leaves to hand-drawing.
rows.theory: After the Sankey diagram (Matthew Sankey, 1898) as popularised by published income-statement visualisations; ADP owns the schema and the etalii/ origin

rows.name: Supply chain diagram

rows.whySpecialized: A supply chain's questions are volume and dependency: bands must widen with what flows through them and a selection must light the whole chain up- and downstream, which a generic canvas leaves to hand-drawing and guesswork.
rows.theory: After the yFiles supply chain showcase ([https://www.yfiles.com/demos/showcase/supply-chain/](https://www.yfiles.com/demos/showcase/supply-chain/)); a notation defined by the user of this repository, so ADP owns the schema and the etalii/ origin

rows.name: Causal loop diagram
rows.purpose: Aims to make the feedback structure of a system explicit, with every loop's reinforcing or balancing label checked against its own arrows.
rows.description: Causal loop diagram (variables joined by polarised causal links, with the feedback loops they form enumerated and labelled `R` or `B` by arithmetic rather than by assertion; `.cld` — ADP’s own line-oriented text format, adopted after XMILE was rejected for carrying stocks, flows and equations this diagram states none of, and carrying one presentation word of its own, `flipped`, which bows a link’s arc to the other side of its chord where the automatic side crosses something); `causal-loop-diagram` (specification removed from the tree; in history before `53f68611`)
rows.whySpecialized: Whether a loop reinforces or balances follows from the signs on its links; a dedicated tool works every loop's label out instead of trusting a hand-drawn R or B.
rows.theory: The notation is the established one from system dynamics — polarity on the link, `R`/`B` on the loop, strokes across a delayed arrow. What ADP adds is the check: a loop is reinforcing on an even count of negative links and balancing on an odd one, so a stated label is verifiable, and a disagreement is reported rather than corrected. Cycles are enumerated with Johnson’s elementary cycles algorithm, bounded. The self-organizing layout adopts Meyer’s method with every source of randomness replaced by a function of the document and the iteration index

rows.description: UML activity diagram (actions, decisions, forks and joins, object flows and partitions)

rows.name: Class diagram
rows.purpose: Model the classes of a system, their attributes and operations, and how they relate.
rows.description: UML class diagram (classes, interfaces, attributes and operations, with associations, generalizations and dependencies)

rows.name: Communication diagram
rows.purpose: Show which objects exchange which numbered messages to carry out one interaction.
rows.description: UML communication diagram (objects and their links, with numbered messages showing the order of an interaction)

rows.name: Component diagram
rows.purpose: Show the components of a system and the interfaces they provide and require.
rows.description: UML component diagram (components, provided and required interfaces, ports and the dependencies between them)

rows.name: Composite structure diagram
rows.purpose: Show the internal parts of a class or component and how they are wired together.
rows.description: UML composite structure diagram (the parts, ports and connectors inside a classifier, and the collaborations they take part in)

rows.name: Deployment diagram
rows.purpose: Show which artifacts are deployed on which nodes and how the nodes communicate.
rows.description: UML deployment diagram (nodes, execution environments, deployed artifacts and communication paths)

rows.name: Interaction overview diagram
rows.purpose: Combine several interactions into one flow of control, like an activity diagram of interactions.
rows.description: UML interaction overview diagram (interactions and interaction uses as nodes in an activity-style flow with decisions and forks)

rows.name: Object diagram
rows.purpose: Show a snapshot of concrete objects, their values and links at one moment.
rows.description: UML object diagram (instances of classes with their slot values and the links between them, at one point in time)

rows.name: Package diagram
rows.purpose: Organize model elements into packages and show the dependencies between them.
rows.description: UML package diagram (packages, their contents, and the import, merge and dependency relationships between them)

rows.name: Profile diagram
rows.purpose: Extend UML for a domain with stereotypes, tagged values and constraints.
rows.description: UML profile diagram (profiles, stereotypes, tagged values and constraints, and the metaclasses they extend)

rows.name: Sequence diagram
rows.purpose: Show the messages between participants in the order they happen.
rows.description: UML sequence diagram (lifelines and the messages between them over time, with combined fragments for loops, alternatives and parallel parts)

rows.name: State machine diagram
rows.purpose: Model the states something can be in and the events that move it between them.
rows.description: UML state machine diagram (states, composite and orthogonal regions, transitions with triggers, guards and effects, and pseudostates)

rows.name: Timing diagram
rows.purpose: Show how the states of participants change along a precise time axis.
rows.description: UML timing diagram (lifelines with their state or value over a time axis, with duration and time constraints)

rows.name: Use case diagram
rows.purpose: Show who uses a system and for which goals.
rows.description: UML use case diagram (actors, use cases, the system boundary, and include, extend and generalization relationships)

rows.name: OWL ontology
rows.purpose: Explore an OWL 2 ontology's classes, hierarchy and restrictions as a VOWL-style graph.
rows.description: OWL 2 ontology (classes, hierarchy, restrictions and axioms in the VOWL vocabulary, asserted-only; an RDF reading over the `w3c/rdf` engine) · `owl-diagram` (specification removed from the tree; in history before `53f68611`)
rows.whySpecialized: OWL axioms are dense in Turtle or RDF/XML; the VOWL notation shows classes, properties and restrictions so an ontology can be checked by eye.

rows.name: RDF graph
rows.purpose: Show the triples of an RDF document as a graph of resources and labelled links.
rows.description: RDF graph (the subjects, predicates and objects of an RDF document drawn as nodes and labelled edges, with prefixes resolved)
rows.whySpecialized: RDF is a graph written down as text; drawing it as one makes missing links, mistyped IRIs and unexpected shapes visible.

rows.name: SHACL shapes
rows.purpose: See which constraints SHACL shapes place on which classes and properties.
rows.description: SHACL shapes graph (node shapes and property shapes, their constraints, and the classes and paths they target)
rows.whySpecialized: Constraints nested in Turtle are hard to follow; a shapes view puts each target, path and constraint side by side.
rows.theory: [W3C SHACL](https://www.w3.org/TR/shacl/) · `shacl-diagram` (specification removed from the tree; in history before `53f68611`)

rows.name: SKOS concept scheme
rows.purpose: Browse and edit a SKOS vocabulary as a hierarchy of concepts with their labels and relations.
rows.description: SKOS concept scheme (concepts with their broader, narrower and related links, top concepts and preferred and alternative labels)
rows.whySpecialized: A thesaurus is a hierarchy with cross-links; a specialized view shows the broader and narrower trees and related links that a flat file hides.
rows.theory: [W3C SKOS reference](https://www.w3.org/TR/skos-reference/) · `skos-diagram` (specification removed from the tree; in history before `53f68611`)

rows.name: SPARQL query
rows.purpose: Read a SPARQL query as the graph pattern it matches, with variables as joins.
rows.description: SPARQL query (`.rq`: the basic graph pattern as a node/edge structure with variables as joins, groups as regions, filters and solution modifiers as annotation and frame; read-only). Deliberately a sibling of the `rdf-diagram` family rather than part of it — a query visualizes asking, not modeling, which is this section's whole distinction · `sparql-diagram` (specification removed from the tree; in history before `53f68611`)
rows.whySpecialized: A basic graph pattern is a shape; drawing it shows at once how variables join and which filters narrow the result.

rows.name: Wardley map
rows.purpose: Map a value chain by how visible each component is to users and how evolved it is.
rows.description: Wardley map (the components of a value chain, placed by their visibility to the user and by their evolution from genesis to commodity, with their dependencies and planned movements)
rows.whySpecialized: The evolution axis puts each component where it is in its life cycle, which is the point of a Wardley map and what a generic diagram leaves out.
rows.theory: [learnwardleymapping.com](https://learnwardleymapping.com/) · reads and writes the [OnlineWardleyMaps .owm DSL](https://onlinewardleymaps.com/), keeping a map another tool wrote byte-for-byte · `wardley-map` (specification removed from the tree; in history before `ece03c36`)

rows.name: Zachman Framework matrix
rows.purpose: Classify an enterprise's architecture descriptions by question and by perspective in the Zachman matrix.
rows.description: Zachman Framework matrix (the six interrogatives what, how, where, who, when and why against the stakeholder perspectives from planner to user)
